controles.affirmation: 'Au premier semestre 2026, MAA a verse 178,1 M$ de dividendes alors que son cash-flow libre n'atteignait que 158,2 M$ (flux operationnels 332,9 M$ moins investissements immobiliers 174,8 M$)'
controles.verbatim_source: Six months ended June 30 : Net cash provided by operating activities 482,549 550,067 ; Purchases of real estate and other assets (46,015) ; Capital improvements and other (167,354) ; Development costs (141,024) ; Dividends paid on common shares (356,923) (354,284) ; Dividends paid on preferred shares (1,844) (10-Q T2 2026, en milliers de $)
controles.correction_proposee: Ces montants sont ceux du SEUL T2 2026, pas du semestre. Sur le S1 2026 le 10-Q donne : flux operationnels 482,5 M$, dividendes actions ordinaires 356,9 M$ (plus 1,8 M$ de preferentielles), investissements immobiliers 354,4 M$. Soit reetiqueter en 'au T2 2026', soit reprendre les chiffres semestriels. Le constat de fond (dividende superieur au cash-flow libre) reste vrai sur le semestre.

controles.affirmation: 'Le Core FFO recule a 502,6 M$ au S1 2026 contre 521,9 M$ au S1 2025, soit -3,7% ; le resultat net progresse pourtant de 12,7% sur la periode'
controles.verbatim_source: Net income 124,818 110,875 251,429 297,281 (trois mois et six mois clos le 30 juin 2026 et 2025, 10-Q T2 2026, en milliers de $)
controles.correction_proposee: Sur le S1 2026 le resultat net RECULE de 15,4% (251,4 M$ contre 297,3 M$). La hausse de 12,6% est celle du seul T2 2026 (124,8 M$ contre 110,9 M$). Ecrire : 'le Core FFO recule de 3,7% sur le semestre alors que le resultat net du seul T2 progresse de 12,6%, porte par des plus-values de cession'.

controles.affirmation: 53,0 M$ verses en deux tranches de 26,5 M$ (mars puis mai 2026) pour regler le recours collectif federal In Re RealPage, qui allegue une entente entre RealPage et environ 50 grands proprietaires dont MAA
controles.verbatim_source: multiple putative class action lawsuits were filed against RealPage, Inc. and approximately 50 of the largest owners and operators of apartment communities in the country, including the Company, alleging that RealPage and such owners and operators conspired to artificially inflate multifamily residential rental prices through the use of RealPage's revenue management software ... the Company was required to pay an aggregate of $53.0 million into a settlement fund ... The settlement payment was made in two equal installments of $26.5 million. The first payment was made in March 2026 and the second payment was made in May 2026. (10-Q T2 2026, Legal Proceedings)

controles.affirmation: Accord de principe distinct de 1,2 M$ avec le procureur du District of Columbia, encore soumis a validation du tribunal
controles.verbatim_source: In July 2026, the Company reached an agreement in principle with the Attorney General for the District of Columbia to settle the DC Litigation against the Company. Under this agreement in principle, the Company will pay the District of Columbia $1.2 million ... This proposed settlement remains subject to the parties' preparation and execution of a Consent Judgment and Order (10-Q T2 2026)

controles.affirmation: La procedure intentee par l'Etat du Kentucky reste en cours et MAA indique avoir l'intention de s'y defendre
controles.verbatim_source: With respect to the Kentucky Litigation, the Company believes there are defenses, both factual and legal, to the allegations in the proceeding and the Company intends to vigorously defend itself. (10-Q T2 2026)
controles.correction_proposee: Ajout possible mais non obligatoire : le reglement de la class action n'a recu qu'une approbation preliminaire le 22 mai 2026, reste soumis a l'approbation definitive du tribunal, et un appel des procureurs generaux DC et Kentucky est pendant devant la Cour d'appel du 6e circuit.

controles.affirmation: 764 M$ de dette a taux variable au 30 juin 2026, soit environ 13% de la dette totale (5,69 Mds $) ; charges d'interets +17,74% contre CA locatif +0,95%
controles.verbatim_source: As of June 30, 2026, we had $764.0 million of variable rate debt outstanding, consisting of $664.0 million under our commercial paper program and $100.0 million under our term loan program. ; Interest expense 53,132 45,111 ; Total debt 5,691,901 (10-Q T2 2026)

controles.affirmation: Loyer effectif moyen Same Store a 1 688 $ contre 1 691 $ un an plus tot ; revenus Same Store -0,31%, NOI Same Store -1,03%, occupation 95,3%

controles.affirmation: Dette nette 5,64 Mds $ au 30 juin 2026 ; Core FFO 502,6 M$ contre 521,9 M$
controles.verbatim_source: Total debt 5,691,901 5,405,372 ; Cash and cash equivalents (51,836) ; Net debt $5,640,065 $5,345,114 ; Core FFO attributable to common shareholders and unitholders 247,524 257,616 502,568 521,878 (10-Q T2 2026)

controles.affirmation: 1 749 logements en developpement ; parc dans 16 Etats ; 10-K : la hausse de l'offre locative pese sur les loyers
controles.verbatim_source: the Company also had six development communities under construction, totaling 1,749 apartment units once complete ... located across 16 states and the District of Columbia as of June 30, 2026 (10-Q T2 2026) ; Our ability to lease our properties at favorable rates is adversely affected by the increase in supply in the multifamily and other rental markets (10-K FY2025, Item 1A)
